content.value_statement: Development sessions are hard to reconstruct after commits, tool changes, and context switches. This skill guides Chronicle session tracking, summaries, search, and Obsidian documentation from one workflow.
actual_capabilities: Guides users to start Chronicle-tracked AI sessions before development begins.
Provides Chronicle CLI commands for sessions, timelines, summaries, and search.
Explains where transcripts, metadata, and the SQLite database are stored locally.
Describes Obsidian documentation handoff for important sessions.
Supports multi-project filtering by repository path and recent work retrieval.
limitations: Requires Chronicle to be installed and configured outside the skill.
Cannot recover full tracking for sessions that were not started through Chronicle.
Obsidian and MCP workflows require related tools or skills to be available.
AI summarization may process transcript content through the configured AI provider.

use_cases.title: Start Clean Tracking
use_cases.description: Start a Chronicle-tracked Claude, Codex, or Claude Code session before feature work begins.

use_cases.title: Review Recent Work
use_cases.description: Use timelines and summaries to understand recent changes, blockers, and follow-up tasks.

use_cases.title: Build Project Memory
use_cases.description: Turn important sessions into Obsidian notes with linked repos, commits, and decisions.

prompt_templates.title: Start a Chronicle Session
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me start a Chronicle-tracked development session for this repository.

prompt_templates.title: Check Tracking Status
prompt_templates.prompt: Check whether this work is tracked by Chronicle and explain what to do next.

prompt_templates.title: Summarize Recent Work
prompt_templates.prompt: Use Chronicle to find my recent work on this project and summarize key decisions.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Project Memory
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a Chronicle workflow for multi-day feature work, including session start, commits, summaries, and Obsidian documentation.

output_examples.input: User asks whether current work is tracked.
output_examples.output: The assistant explains Chronicle only tracks sessions started through Chronicle and recommends restarting before continuing.
The assistant suggests a timeline search, then summarizes sessions, commits, blockers, and next actions.

output_examples.input: User wants documentation after finishing work.
output_examples.output: The assistant routes the session into an Obsidian note with repo, commit, summary, and decision sections.

best_practices: Start Chronicle before work begins so transcripts and metadata are complete.
Commit frequently with clear messages so Chronicle can link sessions to commits.
Document important sessions in Obsidian after summaries are generated.
anti_patterns: Assuming Chronicle can reconstruct a session that was not started through it.
Running browse commands during focused development without user intent.
Treating generated summaries as final records without reviewing key details.

faq.question: Does this skill start tracking automatically?
faq.answer: No. It guides you to start Chronicle before work begins, but Chronicle must be launched explicitly.

faq.question: Can it track old sessions?
faq.answer: No. Chronicle cannot capture a session retroactively.

faq.question: Where is session data stored?
faq.answer: The skill documents Chronicle local storage under ~/.ai-session, including transcripts, metadata, and the SQLite database.

faq.question: Does data leave my machine?
faq.answer: Chronicle stores data locally, but AI summarization may send session content to the configured AI service.

faq.question: Does it require MCP tools?
faq.answer: No. CLI commands are the portable path. MCP tools can make retrieval faster when configured.

faq.question: Can it help with Obsidian notes?
faq.answer: Yes. It points to session documentation workflows and encourages structured project notes with links.
